events.title: The Bonfire of the Vanities in Florence
events.description: Followers of the fiery preacher Girolamo Savonarola gathered in Florence and burned thousands of objects they considered sinful. The pile included cosmetics, mirrors, art and books.
events.significance: It became a lasting symbol of religious zeal turned against art and luxury. It also marked the height of Savonarola's influence over the city.

events.title: Charles Dickens is born
events.description: The future novelist was born in Portsmouth, England. He went on to write Oliver Twist, A Christmas Carol and Great Expectations.
events.significance: Dickens became one of the most widely read authors in the English language. His vivid stories drew attention to poverty and social injustice in Victorian Britain.

events.title: Émile Zola stands trial for libel over 'J'Accuse'
events.description: The celebrated French writer was brought to trial after publishing an open letter that questioned the guilt of army officer Alfred Dreyfus. The letter accused the French establishment of a miscarriage of justice.
events.significance: The trial kept the Dreyfus Affair at the center of French public life. It became a landmark case for the role of intellectuals in challenging state power.

events.title: The Beatles arrive in America
events.description: The band landed at New York's newly renamed John F. Kennedy International Airport, where huge crowds of fans greeted them. Their first US visit set off a wave of Beatlemania.
events.significance: Their arrival launched the British Invasion of American pop music. It reshaped popular culture on both sides of the Atlantic.

events.title: The Maastricht Treaty is signed
events.description: European leaders signed the treaty in the Dutch city of Maastricht, formally creating the European Union. It laid the groundwork for a common currency.
events.significance: The treaty deepened European integration and paved the way for the euro. It reshaped the political and economic landscape of the continent.
